title: Template Literal Types
description: Learn template literal types and the infer keyword for type-level string manipulation.

data.text: Template literal types let you create string types by combining literal types. Combined with the infer keyword, they enable powerful type-level string parsing and manipulation.

data.title: Practical Applications
items: **CSS properties**: Type safe CSS property names
**Slot types**: Extract slot names from component props

data.title: Built-in Helpers
data.text: TypeScript 4.1+ includes Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, and Uncapitalize for working with template literals. Combine them with infer for powerful parsing.

    B --> D[Check: starts with 'on']

items.question: Are template literal types runtime strings?
items.answer: No. They exist only at compile time. The generated JavaScript has no trace of them.

items.question: Can I use them with unions?
items.answer: Yes. Distributive conditional types work with template literals over unions, expanding each member automatically.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Template literals create string patterns at the type level
infer extracts parts of string patterns
Useful for event handlers, routes, and CSS properties
Combined with unions for powerful type parsing
data.takeaway: Template literal types bring string manipulation to TypeScript's type system.
